case_name: Abdul Kadar Mansurmiya Malek v State of Gujarat
respondent:
State of Gujarat
Supreme Court of India

21 August 1997
Cr.A. No. 305 of 1993, Dt. 21 August 1997.
The Order of the Court was as follows:
1.  The appellant was one of the seven accused put up for trial before the Court of Session for offence under Section 302 read with 149 IPC as well for other lesser offences. The trial Court acquitted all the accused. The High Court on appeal at the instance of the State maintained the acquittal of six accused persons other than the appellant. The appeal vis-a-vis the appellant was allowed convicting him for offence under Section 302 IPC sentencing him to life imprisonment. Hence this appeal.
2.  The deceased, Raghunath was a head constable. He along with other police personnel was on duty at the tomb of a Muslim saint where festivities were on, on the night intervening 31st May 1983 and 1st June 1983. facts: The Order of the Court was as follows:... The trial Court acquitted all the accused. The High Court on appeal at the instance of the State maintained the acquittal of six accused persons other than the appellant.

The deceased, Raghunath was a head constable. He along with other police personnel was on duty at the tomb of a Muslim saint where festivities were on, on the night intervening 31st May 1983 and 1st June 1983.

It is alleged that the appellant was friendly with some of those gamblers. It is stated that at that juncture the appellant, present close by in his ice-cream vending truck, came to the spot and gave a knife injury to the deceased in his stomach.

Learned counsel for the appellant made an effort to project that the judgment and order of the Court of Session was far more convincing than that of the High Court, maintaining that the latter Court had committed an error in reversing the well considered judgment of the first Court.

According to him, initially there was an assault by the police inasmuch as its members attempted to catch the supposed gamblers in some of whom the appellant had interest, whereafter the offence by the appellant came to be committed without premeditation in a sudden fight in the heat of passion upon a sudden quarrel and without the appellant having taken undue advantage or acted in a cruel or unusual manner.

On hearing them jointly on this aspect of the matter, we tend to go with them in altering the conviction of the appellant to be under Section 304 Part II IPC under which we sentence him to seven years' imprisonment.

holding: The appeal stands allowed in part. Appeal partly allowed.
